description: Dead-man for the per-camera motion-staleness monitor (binary_sensor.camera_motion_stale / sensor.camera_motion_stale, the recorder-query script). Both its alert and the fleet-wide pipeline check read this sensor's attributes and silently evaluate 'no fault' when it dies. 60 min clears restart windows. RE-ASSERTS hourly (:59) while dead (restart-wipe guard). Covers BOTH death modes: command-level death (state unavailable/unknown) AND the script's fail() path, which emits valid JSON with exit 0 - the sensor stays numeric but its 'error' attribute goes non-null (the problem binary's availability also requires a null error, so that path turns it unavailable as well; dead_err covers it independently of that template). Added 2026-08-17. (2026-10-10: the unavailable/unknown hold is an OR of single-state conditions with for:, because HA 2026.10 rejects for: with a list of states.) 2026-10-28: START-UP CHECK. A state trigger needs a change after it attaches and the dead_err template trigger arms only from a false render, so a monitor that was already dead when Home Assistant started (a Core update, or a deploy followed by a restart, that breaks the script) never fired this alert, and the re-assert restores the card without a push. On the start trigger the run now waits up to 65 min for the monitor to be healthy and pages if it is not; its push says the fault has been present since the start, because the check repeats, once per start, a page sent before the restart. The check runs only on a Home Assistant start: an automation reload that re-arms the triggers while the fault is present is not covered. The hold is 65 min rather than 60 so that the poll 60 min after the first one (scan_interval 30 min) lands inside it; a recorder migration that holds the database for longer at startup pages as the outage it is. camera_monitor_stalled would push an unchanging error payload, or an unknown state, about 105 min after the start (90-min bar plus its 15-min hold). max_exceeded is silent because the :59 re-assert can fall inside the wait; the card then arrives with the push. 2026-10-29: The condition branch 'error is not none' had no hold, so the :59 re-assert created the '60+ min' card on a single erroring poll. Removed: an error makes binary_sensor.camera_motion_stale unavailable (its availability requires error is none), so the held 'unavailable for 60 min' branch already covers it.

then.wait_template: {{ not (states('binary_sensor.camera_motion_stale') in ['unavailable', 'unknown'] or state_attr('sensor.camera_motion_stale', 'error') is not none) }}

then.stop: the monitor was healthy at the start or recovered within the hold
